scenes.say: Two bills arrive for the delivery truck: one for an oil change, one for a new engine. One is an expense. The other goes on the balance sheet.

sub: that keep the asset running: expensed
scenes.say: A revenue expenditure is an ordinary cost that keeps an asset in normal working order: oil changes, tune-ups, new tires. It benefits only the current period, so it's expensed right away.

sub: Extends life, adds capacity or efficiency:
scenes.say: A capital expenditure makes the asset better than it was. It extends its life, increases its capacity, or makes it more efficient. It benefits future periods, so it's capitalized: added to the asset and depreciated.

scenes.heading: The truck's two bills
scenes.say: So the hundred and twenty dollar oil change is repairs expense. The six thousand dollar engine adds three years to the truck's life, so it's capitalized and depreciated over the new remaining life.
The choice matters. Capitalizing a cost that should be expensed overstates assets and this year's profit. WorldCom hid billions of dollars of operating costs exactly that way.

scenes.q: Replacing a warehouse roof that adds 10 years of life is…
scenes.say: Quick check. Replacing a warehouse roof in a way that adds ten years to its life is which kind of expenditure? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B, a capital expenditure. It benefits future periods.

scenes.say: Eventually every asset leaves the business. Sold, traded or scrapped, the disposal follows the same three steps.

scenes.heading: Three steps
items: Remove the cost and accumulated depreciation
Record any cash, and a gain or loss
scenes.say: First, record depreciation up to the date of disposal. Second, remove both the asset's cost and its accumulated depreciation from the books. Third, record any cash received, and the gain or loss.

scenes.heading: Selling old equipment
scenes.say: Redwood River sells equipment that cost eight thousand, with four thousand of accumulated depreciation, so a book value of four thousand. It sells for thirty-five hundred. That's a five hundred dollar loss.

scenes.heading: Record the sale
scenes.say: Debit cash thirty-five hundred. Debit accumulated depreciation four thousand to remove it. Debit loss on sale five hundred. Credit equipment eight thousand.

sub: Scrapped for nothing: loss = book value
scenes.say: Sell for more than book value and you have a gain. Sell for less and you have a loss. If the asset is scrapped for nothing, the loss equals its whole book value. Gains and losses appear below operating income on the multi-step income statement.

scenes.q: Cost $10,000, accumulated depreciation $7,000, sold for $4,000. Result?
scenes.say: Quick check. Cost ten thousand, accumulated depreciation seven thousand, sold for four thousand. What's the result? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's A, a gain of one thousand. Book value is three thousand, and it sold for four.

scenes.say: Depreciation spreads cost gradually. But sometimes an asset loses value suddenly. That's an impairment.
An asset is impaired when its carrying value, cost less accumulated depreciation, can no longer be recovered through using it or selling it.

scenes.heading: Warning signs
items: Physical damage: a flood or fire
A big drop in market value
The asset is used much less than planned
scenes.say: Warning signs include physical damage, like a flood, a sharp fall in market value, new technology that makes the asset obsolete, or a big change in how it's used.

scenes.heading: The grain dryer
scenes.say: A spring flood damages Redwood River's grain dryer. Its carrying value is twenty thousand, but the future cash it can generate won't cover that, and its fair value is now twelve thousand. The impairment loss is eight thousand.

scenes.heading: Record the impairment
scenes.note: Future depreciation is based on the new 12,000 value.
scenes.say: Debit impairment loss eight thousand and credit accumulated depreciation. Future depreciation is then based on the new, lower value. Under US GAAP, the loss can't be reversed if the value later recovers.

scenes.q: After an impairment, depreciation is based on…
scenes.say: Quick check. After an impairment, future depreciation is based on what? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B, the new, lower carrying value.

scenes.say: Dana buys a gravel pit outside town. Every truckload taken out uses up part of the asset. That's depletion.

sub: Timber, minerals, oil and gas, gravel:
assets used up as they are extracted
scenes.say: Natural resources, like timber, minerals, oil and gas, are long-term assets that are physically used up as they're extracted. Spreading their cost is called depletion.

It works like units of production. The pit cost five hundred thousand, and the land should be worth fifty thousand once the gravel's gone. Geologists estimate nine hundred thousand tons. Four hundred fifty thousand over nine hundred thousand tons is fifty cents a ton.
In the first year, Redwood River extracts one hundred twenty thousand tons. Depletion is sixty thousand dollars.

scenes.heading: Record depletion
scenes.note: Becomes cost of goods sold when the gravel is sold.
scenes.say: Depletion is first added to the cost of the gravel inventory. Debit inventory sixty thousand, credit accumulated depletion. When the gravel is sold, that cost becomes cost of goods sold.

scenes.q: Depletion is most like which depreciation method?
scenes.say: Quick check. Depletion works most like which depreciation method? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's C, units of production. Cost is spread by the quantity extracted.

scenes.say: Some of a company's most valuable assets can't be touched: a patent, a brand, a reputation. Here's how accounting handles them.

scenes.heading: Common intangibles
scenes.say: Patents give exclusive rights to an invention, for twenty years from filing. Copyrights protect creative work, for the author's life plus seventy years. Trademarks protect names and logos and can be renewed indefinitely. Then there are franchises and licenses, and goodwill.

scenes.heading: Amortize a patent
scenes.say: Intangibles with a limited life are amortized, usually straight-line, over the shorter of their legal or useful life. Redwood River buys a patent on a feed mixer for thirty thousand, useful for ten years. Debit amortization expense three thousand a year. Credit the patent directly; no accumulated account is usually needed.

sub: Price paid for a business above
the fair value of its net assets
scenes.say: Goodwill arises only when one business buys another and pays more than the fair value of its identifiable net assets. It reflects things like loyal customers and a skilled workforce.

Public companies don't amortize goodwill or other intangibles with indefinite lives. They test them for impairment at least once a year instead. And internally built goodwill is never recorded at all.

scenes.q: When can a company record goodwill?
opts: When it buys another business for more than its net assets
scenes.say: Quick check. When can a company record goodwill? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B. Goodwill is recorded only when it's purchased in an acquisition.

scenes.say: All those long-term asset entries end up in a few lines of the balance sheet, and one ratio tells you how hard they're working.

scenes.heading: Balance sheet presentation
scenes.say: Property, plant and equipment is shown at cost, less accumulated depreciation, to give a net figure. Natural resources and intangibles are shown separately, net of depletion and amortization.

scenes.heading: In the notes
scenes.say: The notes to the financial statements disclose the depreciation methods and useful lives used, the major classes of assets, and any impairments, so readers can compare companies that made different choices.
The asset turnover ratio divides net sales by average total assets. It shows how many dollars of sales each dollar of assets generates.

sub: Each dollar of assets produced $1.45 of sales
scenes.say: If Redwood River had net sales of fifty-eight thousand and average total assets of forty thousand, its asset turnover is one point four five. Each dollar of assets produced a dollar forty-five of sales. Compare it with similar businesses, because it varies a lot by industry.

scenes.q: Net sales $90,000; average total assets $60,000. Asset turnover?
scenes.say: Quick check. Net sales ninety thousand, average total assets sixty thousand. What's the asset turnover? Pause and pick.
